writerSites.buildNoRuledTableCells: the city has no ruled table at all: writes absent-verified with basis.finding 'no ruled setback table exists for <jurisdictionKey>'. The finding says the table is missing; the KIND says the absence was verified. Those are different sentences and the kind is the one readers and gates believe.
writerSites.buildResolvedCells_routerMiss: the city has a table but the code matched no district row (resolved.reason SETBACK_ROUTER_NOT_A_DISTRICT, or SETBACK_ROUTER_NOT_A_TABLE on a repealed Bastrop B3 place type): writes absent-verified with basis.finding SETBACK_ROUTER_NOT_A_DISTRICT. Same inversion.

theDefectAsUnderstood.whyItMatters: absent-verified is an EARNED cell (cell-state.js: EARNED_CELL_KINDS) and is publishable; unaccounted is neither. So 219,472 parcels currently claim a verified absence that no instrument established, and the rail gate reads them as earned rather than as a gap.

theClassificationDesignAndItsProvenance.sourceOfTruthForTheCodeSets: P-255's census, doc_repo scripts/setback-parcel-census.mjs lines 50 and 52, read at source. PLANNED_DEVELOPMENT = /^(PUD|PDD|PD|PC|P-?U-?D)([\s-].*)?$/i, which is the exact formula the dispatch quotes. NON_DISTRICT (the census's own name for the not-applicable candidates) is a single set: /^(|ROW|R\.O\.W\.?|RIGHT[- ]?OF[- ]?WAY|WATER|WATERWAY|STREET|STREETS|HIGHWAY|RAILROAD|NULL|NONE|UNKNOWN|UNZONED|NOT ZONED)$/i.
theClassificationDesignAndItsProvenance.theSplitIAmMakingAndWhy: The census's NON_DISTRICT set is one set for a CANDIDATE report; the census header says so explicitly ('flagged as CANDIDATES for not-applicable, never asserted'). A WRITER has to assert, and the set mixes two different sentences. Split: (a) codes that positively assert the surface is not a zoned parcel, meaning no district schedule can apply, go to not-applicable: blank, ROW, R.O.W., RIGHT-OF-WAY, WATER, WATERWAY, STREET, STREETS, HIGHWAY, RAILROAD. These are the dispatch's own three examples (right-of-way, water, blank) plus the same family. (b) codes that only report that no code is held, and assert nothing about the surface, go to unaccounted naming the raw code: NULL, NONE, UNKNOWN, UNZONED, NOT ZONED. Writing not-applicable for those would be 'checked, none required' in a new spelling, which is the exact defect this row closes. UNZONED and NOT ZONED are the arguable two: if a city's staged layer asserts them as a real attribute they belong in (a), and if the adapter writes them as a fallback for an unreadable code they belong in (b). I could not settle that from this repo (it is parcel-r5-zoning.mjs's and the adapters' question, and the census found zero of them), so I take the honest side (unaccounted, which refuses) and leave the ruling to the operator rather than guessing. See leave_behind in the close.
theClassificationDesignAndItsProvenance.whereTheClassificationAppliesOrder: ONLY inside the router-miss branch (resolved.ok === false). Every code that a table actually resolves is a value and never reaches the classification. That ordering is what makes a false refusal structurally impossible for a city whose table has a real PC, PD, PUD or PDD row.
